summary: Concur splits its surface across host families: a modern v4/SCIM host (base_url, www-{region}.api.concursolutions.com) and several legacy v1.1/v2.0 APIs documented against a different literal host (www.concursolutions.com/api/...). The client must support an absolute-URL path for endpoints on the second family; a regen must not collapse this back to base_url-relative paths.
reason: delegates.list and account.travel were generated with base_url-relative paths guessed from the v4 URI-template pattern (/delegate/v4/delegators, /travelprofile/v2/users/{user_id}). Both 404'd live. developer.concur.com's actual docs place these APIs ('Expense Delegators v1.1', 'Travel Profile v2') on a literal www.concursolutions.com host under /api/... -- a different host and path shape entirely, not a nearby typo. Live-testing the corrected absolute URLs got past the 404 (confirming the path fix) but returned HTTP 401 'Invalid headers' under cookie-session auth for both -- this legacy host does not recognize the modern web-session cookie at all, and both APIs are documented as requiring an OAuth2 Bearer token. This is a genuine, confirmed auth-model boundary, not a bug: cookie-session auth cannot serve either endpoint regardless of further path correction.

changes.description: do()/request building now detects an absolute URL (http:// or https:// prefix) in the resolved path and uses it as-is instead of concatenating onto c.BaseURL. Generically useful for any spec with a multi-host-family API surface, not Concur-specific.
path corrected to the absolute URL https://www.concursolutions.com/api/expense/expensereport/v1.1/delegators (was /delegate/v4/delegators, confirmed 404).

path corrected to the absolute URL https://www.concursolutions.com/api/travelprofile/v2.0/profile (was /travelprofile/v2/users/{user_id}, confirmed 404). Also changed the command from a required <user_id> positional to an optional --user-id flag: the real API's userid_type/userid_value are optional query params, not a required path segment, and omitting them correctly returns the current session user's own profile -- the only identity a cookie-session caller can legitimately request anyway.
resourceReadPaths['delegates'] and resourceDetailPaths['account'] updated to the same absolute URLs, so sync/search do not silently retain the old wrong paths.
syncResourcePath()'s delegates entry updated to match.

validated_outcome: Before: both commands 404'd (wrong host+path entirely). After: both commands reach the real endpoint and get HTTP 401 'Invalid headers' -- the expected, correct response for a cookie session against an OAuth-only legacy API. This is documented in the spec header and per-endpoint descriptions as AUTH-GATED, not silently left broken.
